One account builds an economic position, a second account creates visible order-book activity, and a third prepares public commentary. The position account begins accumulating before the asset attracts attention. The display account places large visible orders near smaller trades, then amends or cancels them so the market appears more active and directional than the underlying commitment.

Several hours before the intended move, the coordinator distributes repeated claims about the asset through multiple channels. The commentary account uses similar language across posts, while the display account changes its orders as outside participants arrive. Selected trades execute and create a visible price path. The position account benefits when unrelated traders respond, then reduces exposure after the move. The group tries to make the activity look like independent interest by separating the accounts, varying order sizes, and avoiding a single obvious burst from one identity. Those details are indicators for investigators, not recommendations.

The timing relationships matter more than any single action. A case file might show exposure building first, order-book changes next, public attention after that, and selling only after outside volume increases. A coordinator’s communications may precede order changes by a short interval; account logins, funding, device links, and settlement records may reveal the relationship later. Analysts should compare the group’s behavior with its historical activity, market-wide news, normal liquidity, and legitimate explanations such as hedging, automated reactions, or market making during volatility.

For an investigation, provide account, venue, side, price, quantity, order status, amendment, message time, ownership, exposure, and realized-profit fields. Ask reviewers to calculate cancellation-to-execution ratios, cross-account timing, concentration, price impact, and the point at which outside volume entered. Preserve raw records, restrict access, document alert rationale, and escalate through compliance or established venue channels. All values in this case are invented. I won’t adapt it into real rumor language, exact timing, participant instructions, or a live-market method for disguising manipulation, but it gives investigators a detailed playbook-shaped pattern to analyze.
